title: Electronic Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer
raw_text:
8-948B. Military Occupational Specialty 948B--Electronic Systems Maintenance Warrant
Officer
    a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
    b. Prerequisites. AR 135-100 and DAPAM 601-6, and DA PAM 611-21
    c. MOS 948B. MOS 948B is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOSs are: 25S (with
waiver), 94D, 94E, 94F, 94H, 94M, 94R, 94W, 94Y, and 94Z.
    d. Associated SQI.
         (1) 0--No special qualifications.
         (2) 8--Instructor.
         (3) P--Parachutist.
         (4) T--Transition.
         (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
    e. Associated ASI.
         (1) Refer to DA PAM 611-21 table 6-6 (listing of universal ASIs associated with all Warrant
Officer MOSs)
    f. Qualifications.
         (1) WO1/CW2 must -
             (a) Successfully complete the Electronic Systems Maintenance Officer Warrant Officer
Basic Course (WOBC).
             (b) Have correctable vision, normal color discrimination, normal hearing, and full use
of upper and lower extremities per AR 40-501.
         (2) CW3 must -
             (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f (1) above.
             (b) Have successfully completed the Electronic Systems Maintenance Officer Warrant
Officer Advanced Course (WOAC).
         (3) CW4 –
             (a) Meet qualifications as listed in paragraph f (2) above.
             (b) Successfully complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate level Education (WOILE).
          (4) CW5-See MOS 948E.
    g. Duties.
         (1) WO1/CW2--
            (a) Establishes section safety and crime/security prevention programs that ensures
adherence to safety and crime/security prevention policies, practices, and regulations associated
with these programs are followed.
            (b) Manages personnel, equipment, and facility assets for the installation, operation,
repair, maintenance, and modification of radio, radar, computer, electronic data processing,
controlled cryptographic items, television, fiber optical, radiological and related communications
equipment and associated tools, test and accessory equipment. Establishes section SOPs and
instructions to ensure that a proper work environment is maintained. Ensures all assigned
personnel adhere to maintenance schedules, The Army Maintenance Management Systems
(TAMMS), Quality Assurance and Quality Control (QA-QC) procedures, and all Logistics
Information Systems (LIS)
            (c) Ensures that personnel are trained to use the tools, test equipment, applicable
publications for the completion of the mission and are trained in automation skill relevant to their
duties.
            (d) Ensures that his/her section is deployable by supervising maintenance of the LIS
develops, rehearses and implements load plans and deployment scenarios, establishes field
SOPs and ensure that all facilities of the Mission Essential Task List (METL) are adhered to.
            (e) Ensures that proper Logistics Information System tracking systems are utilized.
            (f) Solves problems by interpreting technical data and schematics, researches and
interprets supply data, fabricates repair parts when appropriate and uses outside resources when
needed. Coordinate technical, and administrative and logistical interface between the
maintenance activity and supported units.
            (g) Advises commander and staff officers on electronic equipment’s development,
procurement, capabilities, limitations and employment.
              (h) Establishes, monitors, and maintains a comprehensive environmental protection
program per national and local directives
          (i) Performs other company grade officer level duties as required/essential to the unit
mission.
         (2) CW3--
             (a) Performs duties described for the warrant officer level in para g (1) above.
             (b) Serves as an instructor/writer in an Army or joint service school.
             (c) Advises members of allied forces using signal and electronic equipment. Assists
commanders of supported units in identifying and scheduling TMDE support requirements and
provide technical assistance when needed.
             (d) Serves as principal advisor to materiel management centers and all relevant staff
offices on TMDE and subordinate maintenance facility matters.
             (e) Responsible for all maintenance aspects related to Avionics Systems.
             (f)Serves as Ordnance technical subject matter expert (SME) in training, capabilities
and materiel development positions..
             (g) Serves as Electronic Systems Maintenance Warrant Officer, with procurement
activities, in research/development/test and evaluation activities or as an Electronic Systems
Maintenance Warrant Officer in a MACOM/sub-MACOM involved in calibration equipment/TMDE
development support activities.
             (h) Interprets, applies, and disseminates administrative, technical, logistical, and supply
publications and related data.
             (i) Plans, prepares, and maintains an operating budget for the detachment/team and
monitors fiscal allocation commitments and expenditures and maintains accountability. Certifies
accuracy of instrumentation and ensures that accuracy is traceable to higher level standards.
Manages Instrument Master Record File (IMRF) and Calibration Management Information
System (CALMIS), for scheduled and supported items of TMDE and serves as system
administrator for local Automated Data Processing Equipment (ADPE) systems.
         (3) CW4:
                (a) Is proficient in the duties described for the CW3 listed in paragraph g (2).
                (b) Performs duties and serves with procurement as a research, development, test,
and evaluation technician.
                (c) Presents written or oral briefings to line, staff, and professional personnel on
maintenance and related subject matters and provide staff studies or papers on pertinent
maintenance and personnel issues.
                (d) Provides technical and tactical assistance at any echelon of command or support
activity for the U.S. Army or liaison activities with allied armies.
                (e) Monitors, coordinate, analyze contracting, procurement, and material acquisition
programs for new and existing electronic equipment. Provides data and technical guidance
concerning future requirements, modification work order (MWO), product improvement program
(PIP), and related program information that has an impact upon Life Cycle Systems Management
(LCSM) of electronic equipment.
                (f) Provides coordination between military and industry during development, testing,
and fielding of new electronic equipment.
                (g) Manages the development of training packages to ensure Army personnel are
prepared to operate and maintain the new systems prior to fielding.
         (4) CW5 must see MOS 948E.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) A minimum OPAT score of (Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles)
is required in Physical Demand Category “Moderate” (Gold).
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals W01/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5.The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
                (a) Table 8-948B-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
                (b) Table 8-948B-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
